messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Name: [Patient Name]
Medical Record Number: [MRN]

Admission Date: [Admission Date]
Discharge Date: [Discharge Date]

History of Present Illness:
The patient, a 53-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and dyslipidemia, underwent laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with D3 lymphadenectomy for moderately differentiated tubular adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. Postoperative surveillance revealed a 23-mm sessile polyp at the superior rectum, which was successfully removed by endoscopic mucosal resection. 39 months after EMR, a mass lesion was found in the presacral area on CT as postoperative surveillance. The patient underwent LAR with D3 lymphadenectomy, and the recurrent site was completely removed without adjuvant chemotherapy.

Hospital Course:

Admission:
The patient was admitted for LAR with D3 lymphadenectomy due to presacral lymph node recurrence of rectal cancer.

Treatment:
The patient underwent LAR with D3 lymphadenectomy, and the recurrent site was completely removed by surgery.

Clinical Progress:
The postoperative course was uneventful, and he was discharged from our hospital on postoperative day 11.

Discharge Condition:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was discharged home in stable condition.

Instructions:
The patient should follow up with his primary care physician and oncologist for postoperative surveillance per their recommendations.

Signed,
[Physician Name]
[Title]

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Surgery this admission targeted a presacral lymph node recurrence of rectal cancer, i.e. metastatic disease in intrapelvic lymph nodes, after the rectal primary had been resected endoscopically. When treatment is directed at the secondary site, the secondary neoplasm is sequenced as principal. This falls in chapter C, secondary malignant neoplasm of lymph nodes (intrapelvic), category C77.

CODE: C77
